g.text: * Counts: tools, resources, resource templates, prompts
From a run without credentials, `ready` means the server let MCPJam connect and list without a token. It does not mean every tool
is public: a server can still ask for sign-in when a protected tool is called. To check, call that tool with `mcpjam tools call`.
A 401 challenge fails the call with `AUTH_REQUIRED`, and its details name the `mcpjam oauth login` command to run. A ChatGPT-style
challenge returns the tool result with `_authChallenge` next to it. See [Mid-session sign-in](https://docs.mcpjam.com/inspector/l
The `--out <path>` flag writes the full JSON artifact to a file, useful for handoff to another engineer or agent.
For stdio targets, those artifacts only record the explicit env keys you passed
via `-e/--env`; inherited shell variables are not enumerated.
Credential headers (`Authorization`, `X-Api-Key`, `X-Auth-Token`, and any other sensitive header names) are automatically redacted
to `[REDACTED]` in all printed output and written artifacts, including RPC logs attached via `--rpc`. Header names are preserved
so the request shape remains visible.
Get initialization info for a connected server.
Returns the server's `serverInfo` (name, version) and `capabilities` from the MCP initialize response.
Connect to a server and verify the debugger surface works.
Export a full snapshot of the server's tools, resources, prompts, and capabilities as JSON.
